fixes.after:
Three devices A, B and C are connected to the bus of a computer, input/output transfers for all three devices use interrupt control. Three interrupt request lines INTR1, INTR2 and INTR3 are available with priority of $\text{INTR}_1 >$ priority of $\text{INTR}_2 >$ priority of $\text{INTR}_3$.

Draw a schematic of the priority logic, using an interrupt mask register, in which Priority of A > Priority of B > Priority of C.

fixes.before: Daisy-chain priority resolution: Device A has highest priority, followed by B, then C
fixes.after: Parallel priority logic: A, B, C drive INTR1, INTR2, INTR3; each request is ANDed with its mask-register bit ($I_k = R_k M_k$), then priority gating gives $G_A = I_1$, $G_B = \overline{I_1}I_2$, $G_C = \overline{I_1}\,\overline{I_2}I_3$, and INT to the CPU $= \text{IEN}\cdot(I_1 + I_2 + I_3)$; the grant/encoder output selects the vector of the highest-priority unmasked device
fixes.reason: The stored "daisy chain" answer ignores the interrupt mask register and the three separate INTR lines the question specifies; the intended design is mask-register gating + priority logic.
